::: {#exm-average-fit-auto}

#### The expected prediction of a line on cylinders

Treat the 392 cars of the `Auto` data [@james2021islr2e] as the whole world of cars.
A [training set](#def-training-set) is 30 cars drawn at random from it, and the learning algorithm fits the line of `mpg` on `cylinders`.
Draw 2000 [training sets](#def-training-set), fit a line to each, and record each line's [intercept](correlation-regression.qmd#def-slr-intercept), [slope](correlation-regression.qmd#def-slr-slope) and [prediction](prediction.qmd#def-prediction) at 4 cylinders.
Both tabs draw with the `SyncRNG` package [@vandenburg2024syncrng], a random number generator with the same algorithm in R and Python, from the same seed, so they pick the same cars:

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Python

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from SyncRNG import SyncRNG

auto_af = pd.read_csv("data/auto.csv").dropna(subset=["horsepower"])
cyl_af = auto_af["cylinders"].to_numpy(float)
mpg_af = auto_af["mpg"].to_numpy(float)

rng_af = SyncRNG(seed=1)
coefs_af = np.empty((2000, 2))
for s_af in range(2000):
    # One training set: the first 30 rows of a shuffle of all the rows (Python counts from 0), and the line fitted to it.
    pick_af = rng_af.shuffle(list(range(len(mpg_af))))[:30]
    slope_af, intercept_af = np.polyfit(cyl_af[pick_af], mpg_af[pick_af], 1)
    coefs_af[s_af] = intercept_af, slope_af

preds_af = coefs_af[:, 0] + coefs_af[:, 1] * 4

# The expected prediction at 4 cylinders is the mean of those predictions.
# The Monte Carlo standard error of that mean is the spread of the predictions over sqrt(2000).
mc_se_af = preds_af.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(2000)
print(preds_af.mean().round(2), preds_af.min().round(2), preds_af.max().round(2), mc_se_af.round(3))
```

### R

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
auto_af <- read.csv("data/auto.csv")
auto_af <- na.omit(auto_af[, c("mpg", "cylinders", "horsepower")])

# SyncRNG is a random number generator with the same algorithm
# in R and Python, so the draws match the Python tab.
library(SyncRNG)
rng_af <- SyncRNG(seed = 1)
coefs_af <- t(replicate(2000, {
  # One training set: the first 30 rows of a shuffle of all the rows,
  # and the line fitted to it.
  rows <- rng_af$shuffle(seq_len(nrow(auto_af)))[1:30]
  coef(lm(mpg ~ cylinders, data = auto_af[rows, ]))
}))

preds_af <- coefs_af[, 1] + coefs_af[, 2] * 4

# The expected prediction at 4 cylinders is the mean of those predictions.
# The Monte Carlo standard error of that mean is the spread of the
# predictions over sqrt(2000).
mc_se_af <- sd(preds_af) / sqrt(2000)
summary_af <- c(
  mean = mean(preds_af),
  min = min(preds_af),
  max = max(preds_af)
)
c(round(summary_af, 2), mc_se = round(mc_se_af, 3))
```

:::

No single [training set](#def-training-set) produces the [expected prediction](#def-average-fit).
The 2000 lines [predict](prediction.qmd#def-prediction) anywhere from `r sprintf("%.1f", min(preds_af))` to `r sprintf("%.1f", max(preds_af))` miles per gallon for a four-cylinder car,
and their mean, `r sprintf("%.1f", mean(preds_af))`, is the expected prediction $\avgfitf{4}$ of @eq-average-fit,
with a 95% Monte Carlo [confidence interval](inference.qmd#def-confidence-interval) of `r sprintf("%.2f", mean(preds_af) - 1.96 * mc_se_af)` to `r sprintf("%.2f", mean(preds_af) + 1.96 * mc_se_af)`
(1.96 Monte Carlo [standard errors](estimation.qmd#def-SE) either side).
The two tabs print the same numbers up to rounding.

@fig-average-fit-auto plots 100 of the 2000 lines, their pointwise average, and the true [mean function](#def-mean-function):

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Python

```{python}
#| label: fig-average-fit-auto
#| fig-cap: "The fitted lines of 100 of the 2000 training sets (grey), their pointwise expected prediction (blue), and the true mean function (orange), for `mpg` against `cylinders`."
#| fig-alt: "A plot of miles per gallon against cylinders, from 3 to 8. One hundred faint grey lines slope downward and fan out, most widely at 3 and 8 cylinders and most narrowly between 6 and 7 cylinders. A thick blue line, the average of all 2000 fitted lines, runs down through the middle of the grey lines. A thick orange line with points at 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 cylinders, the mean mpg of the cars with that many cylinders, is not straight: it starts well below the blue line at 3 cylinders, rises above it at 4 and 5, and then follows it down to 8. A legend below the plot names the three: one fitted line, expected prediction, and true mean function."
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

grid_af = np.arange(3, 9)
# The pointwise expected prediction is the mean of the fitted lines at each cylinder count.
avg_af = (coefs_af[:, [0]] + coefs_af[:, [1]] * grid_af).mean(axis=0)
# The true mean function is the mean mpg of the cars with each cylinder count.
truth_af = auto_af.groupby("cylinders")["mpg"].mean()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5), layout="constrained")
for intercept_af, slope_af in coefs_af[:100]:
    ax.plot(grid_af, intercept_af + slope_af * grid_af, color="grey", alpha=0.3, linewidth=0.8)
# One legend entry for the 100 grey lines, with a solid line to stand for them.
ax.plot([], [], color="grey", label="One fitted line (100 shown)")
ax.plot(grid_af, avg_af, color="steelblue", linewidth=2.5, label="Expected prediction")
ax.plot(truth_af.index, truth_af.values, color="darkorange", linewidth=2.5, marker="o", label="True mean function")
ax.set_xlabel("cylinders")
ax.set_ylabel("miles per gallon")
fig.legend(loc="outside lower center", ncol=3, frameon=False)
plt.show()
```

### R

```{r}
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A plot of miles per gallon against cylinders, from 3 to 8.
#|   One hundred faint grey lines slope downward and fan out,
#|   most widely at 3 and 8 cylinders
#|   and most narrowly between 6 and 7 cylinders.
#|   A thick blue line, the average of all 2000 fitted lines,
#|   runs down through the middle of the grey lines.
#|   A thick orange line with points at 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 cylinders,
#|   the mean mpg of the cars with that many cylinders, is not straight:
#|   it starts well below the blue line at 3 cylinders,
#|   rises above it at 4 and 5, and then follows it down to 8.
#|   A legend below the plot names the three:
#|   one fitted line, expected prediction, and true mean function.
library(ggplot2)

grid_af <- 3:8
# One row per fitted line and cylinder count;
# the pointwise expected prediction is the mean over lines.
lines_af <- data.frame(
  line = rep(seq_len(nrow(coefs_af)), each = length(grid_af)),
  cylinders = grid_af,
  fit = as.vector(t(coefs_af[, 1] + outer(coefs_af[, 2], grid_af)))
)
avg_af <- aggregate(fit ~ cylinders, data = lines_af, FUN = mean)
# The true mean function is the mean mpg of the cars with each cylinder count.
truth_af <- aggregate(mpg ~ cylinders, data = auto_af, FUN = mean)

line_name_af <- "One fitted line (100 shown)"
avg_name_af <- "Expected prediction"
truth_name_af <- "True mean function"

ggplot() +
  geom_line(
    data = subset(lines_af, line <= 100),
    aes(cylinders, fit, group = line, colour = line_name_af),
    alpha = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = avg_af,
    aes(cylinders, fit, colour = avg_name_af),
    linewidth = 1.5
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = truth_af,
    aes(cylinders, mpg, colour = truth_name_af),
    linewidth = 1.5
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = truth_af,
    aes(cylinders, mpg, colour = truth_name_af),
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("grey60", "steelblue", "darkorange"),
    breaks = c(line_name_af, avg_name_af, truth_name_af)
  ) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1))) +
  labs(x = "cylinders", y = "miles per gallon", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
